plan: Store the workspace as the deep-copied input dictionary; a single mutable tree is the only state, so to_data() is simply another deep copy.

Provide one recursive generator that yields every item in document order; build total_word_count, unresolved_markers, and outline on top of it so all kinds are processed uniformly at any nesting depth.
Count note words by first stripping [[?identifier]] markers with a regex, then counting \b\w+\b runs; add each reference's declared word_count.
Collect marker identifiers from note text (regex capture) and from reference 'unresolved' lists into a set, returned sorted.
Render the outline as the workspace title plus one line per item: two spaces per nesting level (top-level items at depth 1) followed by '<kind>: <title>'.

Implement move as validate-then-mutate: check id types, locate the item and its parent list, resolve the destination ('workspace' literal or a section/group), reject non-containers, reject self/descendant destinations via an identity-based subtree scan, and range-check the insertion index — all before any mutation, guaranteeing failed moves leave the tree untouched.
Ship embedded unittest tests that build fixtures in memory and assert the queries, the exact outline, a successful move, and that every rejection path leaves to_data() exactly unchanged.
mechanisms: Recursive part-whole tree of plain dictionaries (sections/groups contain items; notes/references are leaves)
Single document-order generator shared by all aggregate operations
Regex marker stripping before word tokenization
Set-union marker collection with lexicographic sort
Validate-before-mutate atomic move with containment/no-cycle check
Deep-copy isolation at construction and export
